artifacts.summary: Recommends adding a 9-tool mcp__playwright__* permission enumeration via a new agent-system/extensions/web/settings-fragment.json + manifest merge_targets.settings entry, deployed to .claude/settings.local.json (not install-once), which is the confirmed sanctioned mechanism for reaching already-initialized projects.

memory_candidates.content: In this repo's extension-loader system, `merge_targets.settings` in an extension's manifest.json (source: settings-fragment.json, target: .claude/settings.local.json) is deployed via process_merge_targets/merge_settings (init.lua/merge.lua), a completely separate code path from loader.lua's copy_category. It performs an additive, idempotent deep-merge (never overwrites existing scalars, dedups array items via vim.deep_equal) and is NOT gated by the install_once flag, which applies only to the root_files category (core/root-files/settings.json). This is the sanctioned way to add permission grants that must reach an already-initialized project -- confirmed independently by check-extension-docs.sh's check_settings_merge_source_coverage rationale.

MCP permission grants should prefer a wildcard (mcp__{server}__*) over enumeration EXCEPT when a server intentionally splits its tool surface into a safe/always-allow tier and an unsafe/always-prompt tier (e.g. Playwright's browser_navigate/browser_click/etc. vs browser_evaluate/browser_run_code_unsafe/browser_file_upload). In that case enumeration of only the safe tools is required, not technical debt -- a wildcard would silently re-grant the unsafe tools too.

Three code paths trigger an extension's merge_targets.settings re-merge in this repo's extension loader: (1) manager.load(name) on a not-yet-loaded extension, (2) manager.reload(name), which unloads then loads a single named extension, and (3) the picker's 'Reload All' bulk resync, which calls manager.load(name, {force=true}) for every already-active extension (bypassing the is_loaded short-circuit) rather than unloading everything first. Any of the three picks up new settings-fragment.json entries.
